correctness.rationale: Nilpotent resolvent multiplication gives diagonal 1/D and shear β(t+2v)/D² with D=1+t+v, where the quadratic for the normalized durations realizes all v∈[0,t²/4]. The largest singular value gives the stated objective. The sign of its log derivative is the sign of β(t+2) minus an increasing radical, excluding interior minima (including the zero-shear case). The equal/sparse norm ratio increases strictly in y=βt, from d/c²<1 to d²/c³ (d=1+t, c=1+t/2). At t=1+√5 the limiting ratio equals one but is never reached at finite β. Below it there is exactly one crossing; equating the inverted singular-value equations and substituting gives the squared threshold and its strictly positive derivative, independently checked. Continuity plus the strict exclusion of interior minima gives precisely the two tie multisets and the open-simplex infimum. The example reproduces 0.853850937603 versus 0.860179616570 despite negative symmetric part. The generator is scalar, not defective, at s=0; this wording does not affect the formula or theorem.
residual_risks: Numerical checks do not establish all horizons or shears; those cases are handled by the derivative and ratio arguments.

value.rationale: This is the minimal nonnormal allocation problem with competing scalar damping and shear. A complete best-design classification is useful as a benchmark because equal steps can lose even for an energy-dissipative generator, and no positive unequal step design can improve the two extremal policies.
residual_risks: The criterion is numerical damping, not approximation error, computational work or general multistage performance.
